title: The Weight of Here
summary: Settling into the body and the sounds around you, one moment at a time.
reflectionQuestion: Where in your day today could you stop for three breaths?

transcript.text: Before anything else, notice that you've stopped. Whatever came before this can wait a few minutes.
Let your body settle into whatever is holding it. The chair, the floor, the bed. Let it take a little more of your weight.
Breathe in through your nose, a little slower than usual. And let the breath go, without pushing it out.
Now let the breath do whatever it wants. You don't need to manage it.
Notice where your hands are. Feel their weight. Maybe the temperature of the air on the backs of them.
Notice your feet. Whether they're touching the ground, or a blanket, or each other.
Now listen. Start with the sounds furthest away. Traffic, wind, a distant voice, or just the hum of the building.
Then the sounds in the room. And then the quietest sound you can find. Perhaps your own breathing.
Thoughts will come too. A list, a conversation, something you forgot. That's not a mistake.
When you notice you've drifted, that moment of noticing is the practice. Just come back to the feeling of sitting here.
For the next little while, there's nothing to do but be here. If your attention wanders, bring it home to your body, as often as you need.
Begin to let a little movement come back. Perhaps your fingers, or a slow roll of the shoulders.
As you go into your day, see if you can find one moment to stop like this again, even for three breaths.
Waiting for the kettle. Standing at a door. Before you answer a message.
Whenever you're ready, open your eyes, and arrive.
